recent_reviews.author: Bob Davies
recent_reviews.text: The next patients' group meeting is on the 6th of May at 5pm. We established that patients can arrive a little early (say 10 minutes) to discuss individual problems/experience, so the PPG can focus clearly on shared problems. Whether you can attend or not, please write your review, good or bad, and I will continue to bring them to the new team. From the PPG meeting on Feb 4th... The practice is fully staffed for doctors (now at 6, and 6 admin) but doesn't have a practice manager as they're having trouble recruiting because they will also manage the Oldham practice. I have been assured they're wiring up a better fallback after 2 missed calls (most likely you will receive a text that asks you to ring the practice, but I have asked that a bookable slot picker be added too). The website is now 24hr accessible for admin/repeats, but still cannot be used out of office hours to request an appointment. The doctor has concerns about people using it for 'urgent' requests in the middle of the night (when no doctor is available to receive it), I've tried to make a case for it, but if out of hours appointment-requests is a blocker for you, please come to meetings and help me argue the case. I have also reraised when tests come back all green, but you're still sick, the practice currently close your diagnosis process until you re-engage (which you may not be told you need to do), which I intend to reraise in future. --- From the PPG meeting on November 26th... 2 new doctors are on board, and new staff are coming soon. Complaints about reception seem to be improving, less reliance on agency staff. The website will be switched to 24hr accessible. New Bank is on Bookable, which is much easier to use and is currently accessible outside of office hours (unlike PATCHS), but doesn't work for existing registered patients, and only has a limited number of slots and is only for booking an appointment. --- From the PPG meeting on 10th of September. The practice is moving to a new digital system on 1st of October, which 'should' solve some of the current technical issues with arranging appointments. Management say there will be some onboarding help and open/group sessions for anybody who would like to attend, and dates/times of those will be on a notice-board in the reception (or from Lynne, the operations manager) once those dates are arranged (probably a couple of evenings/saturdays depending on demand). We have also been assurred the quality of help from reception has been better in the last month and will continue to improve. There is still no new practice manager. They are recruiting for one in a difficult market, but they are adding new administrators (from October 6th, if I understood correctly) and _should_ soon be adding extra doctors too, with a less clear timescale (presumably notice-period related). The patient load on doctors is within the normal NHS range, so do not put off making an appointment just because you think they're busy, they have capacity and are adding more, and most of the problems seem to be steadily improving. --- After leaving a previous 1 star review with many negative points and being frustrated with being unable to arrange an appointment, I attended the newly set-up Patient Participation Group meeting (as a new management company took over in April) on 6th August. The discussion between the team and a few patients was constructive and the new management team seem to have an understanding of the problems after we explained in some detail. I also brought these reviews to their attention, and provided a breakdown of reviews to their management in the meeting. If you're here because you've had a negative experience, either recently or before the take-over, we've been assured they're working on it and should be moving to a new system, as well as dealing with the problems caused by specific staff. Please contact management with feedback and come to the patient meeting if you have the time, be heard, the new team are (it seems) finally listening, and they actually have a mandate to fix problems atm.

recent_reviews.author: Joyce Louis
recent_reviews.text: I'm extremely disappointed with the recent changes at this GP surgery. I had a blood test scheduled but was given a date I couldn’t attend. When I managed to make time, the appointment was cancelled due to "unforeseen circumstances." The new system for ordering medication is also a step backward. It was previously simple to order through the pharmacy app, but now it's linked to the NHS app, which requires identity verification. Despite submitting my details, I'm told it will take several days for confirmation—followed by additional delays for dispensing and delivery. This puts me at risk of running out of essential medication, which is unacceptable. This level of service is deeply concerning. I will be looking to move to a more reliable GP surgery.

recent_reviews.author: Javad Moazami
recent_reviews.text: Rating: 1/5 - Extremely DisappointingService Unfortunately, my experience at this clinic was very unpleasant. The behavior of the reception team was seriously unprofessional and disrespectful. On several occasions, they were either absent or busy with other tasks, leaving me waiting for long periods without any guidance. I was never informed that I needed to use the automated check-in system, and even if I had been informed, I would have required assistance. When I encountered disrespectful and insulting behavior, none of the reception staff paid attention to the issue, which caused significant distress and psychological pressure. It seems that the clinic manager is not paying attention to these problems and is not hearing the voices of patients. After sharing this review, I was surprised (and somewhat saddened) to find that several others had similar experiences at this clinic. Given how often such stories seem to come up, it might be worth taking a closer look—not just for me, but for others who may be facing similar situations. In fact, what I’m about to describe is only one of several upsetting experiences I’ve had at this clinic—and sadly, not the last. I am not sure whether this was racially motivated, but the way I was treated was deeply inhumane. I begged them to inform my doctor—who had been regularly renewing my weekly prescription for over a year—that I had run out of critical medication. They completely ignored me and, instead of offering help, shouted at me to leave the clinic. At that very moment, I briefly saw my doctor through a door behind one of the senior staff members—she appeared to say something to someone at a desk and then turned back and disappeared. Still, the staff insisted she wasn’t there. When I told one of the senior team members—who seemed to be in charge or at least more experienced than the others—what I had seen, she and her colleagues pointed at me, laughed at my desperation, and mocked me while I stood there in distress. After being kicked out of the clinic, I walked away with tears in my eyes, feeling utterly humiliated, unwanted, and hopeless. I was in a mental health crisis, and the lack of compassion pushed me to a point where I genuinely started thinking about ending my life. The pain of that moment hasn’t left me—it replays in my mind every single day. The medication that helped me cope was gone, and so was my sense of dignity. And this wasn’t the only time I was treated poorly. I had endured other incidents of disrespect and mistreatment before, but I didn’t know who to turn to or how to raise my concerns. So I kept silent. Eventually, I found the courage to tell my doctor honestly and emotionally what had been happening—only to be removed from the GP a few days later. No one should ever be made to feel that way in a place that is supposed to provide care.

recent_reviews.author: Shadow S
recent_reviews.text: This practice is one of the worst practices going. It USED TO BE good, offering same day appointments as stated on their website as long as we fill in the form within the designated time. But now it’s going downhill and after reading other reviews and realising I’m not the only one it’s made me feel even more frustrated. I filled a form in a couple weeks ago and I called up to make sure they’re received my form and they’ll be offering me an appointment the same day. The receptionist told me the doctor has received my form and will definitely call me back that same day. I waited and waited, I was so ill I fell asleep and when I woke up I realised they’re closed, I double checked my call logs and I didn’t receive a single call. This has happened to me before where I’ve been ignored by them which is why I called up this time to make sure they’ll definitely call me back. The receptionist falsely reassured me that the doctor would “definitely” call me back that same day. I felt I had an infection and needed antibiotics but they didn’t even bother. I needed an emergency appointment. I waited another day thinking they might’ve been busy but still no call back, I ended up getting better on my own without any support from the gp. I had to call in sick to work as I didn’t have any medication to make me better any sooner. I’ve been feeling ill again for the past week and I’ve not even bothered filling a form in or calling up to book an appointment because of how bad the service is and as I know I’ll just be neglected yet again. This isn’t how one should feel when in need of support. This practice really needs to fix up and get rid of all the slackers.

recent_reviews.text: The worst GP in Manchester. The appointments system is from 1965, where you have to wake up at 6am and file in the form online, or else they are closed by 8am. And then you sit until next day in pain without medication. If you fill the form for referal, they need 6 weeks to get it ready. Receptionists sit there and just talk to each other and do not answer calls, making you wait on hold for 35 mins at a time. But when you visit the GP, its always pin drop empty. Many times I've put a form in requesting to speak to my doctor I don't get through to her straight away when she's told me many times all I need to do is send her a message when I told her i do she told me she hadn't recieved it, so I started being adamant in my appointment requests that I want to speak to my Dr. I have filled in a feedback form and am still waiting to hear back from Andrew Gee or Lauren, but nothing, I'll probably have better luck getting Lauren to reply back to this post than my feedback form! When it clearly states on the website that if you have a complaint to fill in a feedback form or alternatively call to book an appointment, but when I called I was told the only way was to fill in a form (maybe because they know they can ignore your form!) I have been told to appeal a decision that I hadn't even received in writing, I've asked for a formal letter from them so I can complain to nhs England but still haven't recieved the letter because they don't want me to complain to nhs England or the ombudsman, but I will be going ahead with my complaints.

recent_reviews.author: John Mccormack
recent_reviews.text: Only recently moved to this general practice and I regret moving at all. I’d prefer the 40 minute drive to my previous GPs over the below woeful experiences the last several weeks. Attached image of a confirmation text from the GPs. Booked the morning off work, arrive to the appointment to be told I’m booked in for September. Today is Friday the 15th August. Not Monday the 15th September. Secondly, advised over the phone to register my daughter for the GPs I’ll need to come physically into the building to scan a QR code that isn’t on the website. Scanned, completed and registered. Popped in to see if this has progressed as we’ve heard nothing - nothing on the system, come in with your child to register her. Another morning off work. Finally, the biggest disaster - I’ve had a kidney stone for several weeks, agonising pain. Hospital discharged me with a scan booked that due to a motorway accident I couldn’t attend (things happen, life…). I ended up back in hospital again with kidney pain and was advised to raise with my GP to rebook a scan, raised via patches and requested “update via telephone” (though I’m not sure why you’d bother given they’ll either just update in patches with no notification to you or text, they don’t honour the requested means of contact). No update for a week, I log into patches to find the request has been cancelled due to “more information required” from the GP. Bear in mind the request outlines a doctor at the hospital has outlined I require a kidney scan and to request this from the GPs. Symptoms = kidney pain likely stones (not confirmed yet as need the scan, could be more malicious!) and noted worsening pain. I raise another patches request and am advised to come in later that week. At this point I’ve no more tramadol a new born baby and I can’t move. I’ve rang the GP to ask for help, they advised ring 111, I ring 111 who advise speak to the GP. 111 ring the GP who advise they can’t see me today, so I end up back in hospital. With agonising pain. Avoid entirely. I’ll be moving myself, my partner and our child to another GPs that doesn’t have such shocking reviews. And I can see why. One gentleman behind the reception counter is genuinely lovely and helpful, one male doctor (with a slight lisp, apologies on the description but credit due where credit is due his expertise and professionalism were exceptional and I don’t know his name!) the rest of the staff that I have encountered should take note of the above as my experiences have been of incompetence, unhelpful, rude, demeaning and frustrated tones over the phone. Almost as though it’s somehow MY fault information isn’t being passed between health care “professionals” via hospital > GP and / or completed forms disappearing into the void. The reception staff (excluding the outlined gentleman above) are the embodiment of “every GP receptionist thinks they are a medical expert”. This practise would be laughable if it wasn’t a case of people’s lives and welfare at stake. More than embarrassing, an utter disgrace.

recent_reviews.text: Every time I stopped myself from leaving a review, but this time was the last straw. I don’t know if they deliberately test and hire the rudest, most emotionless people as receptionists, but it certainly feels that way. If someone lacks empathy and basic human decency, they should not be working in healthcare. I have witnessed their extreme rudeness not only towards myself but also towards others—including a 90-year-old man! They have no idea what empathy means. When I contacted them for my appointment last month, they were incredibly rude to me. Today, when I called twice regarding my father, the only response I got was: "Go to a walk-in centre." I explained that I had just returned from there and simply wanted an appointment with a doctor—tomorrow or on any available day. I asked if they were seriously telling me to go and wait another six hours, and shockingly, they said, "YES." I truly hope no one has to deal with this place or their staff. While the doctors are amazing, the receptionists make the experience unbearable.

recent_reviews.author: Devon Tynan
recent_reviews.text: Shocking GP service. I have been a patient here since being a child, I’m now 24 and only in the last year or 2 has this GP service really gone down hill. My main concern at this GP practice is a fairly new member of reception staff called Farzana, she is extremely rude and unhelpful. I recently rang to review my sons records he had blood tests 6 months prior to this phone call where she told me there was a problem with my sons blood results and I needed to make an appointment with a doctor to discuss these where she offered me an appointment for in 3 weeks time. I went to the GP practice to collect a copy of his blood results so I could see which of his bloods were out of range, when I got there she told me I couldn’t collect my 6 year olds blood results without ID, this is not GP policy you only need ID to collect somebody else’s results if they are over 16. I demanded my sons bloods were reviewed by somebody clinical that day as six months had gone by since the bloods were done. Farzana was extremely argumentative. Another receptionist heard and was helpful and understanding and went and got a nurse to review his bloods. The nurse reassured me and said his bloods had been put as no action by a doctor which was completely different to what Farzana had told me on the phone. Farzana did not apologise for the mistake she had made or the panic and upset she had caused me. A couple of weeks later I had to ring again after my son had been bit by a dog, I asked if she could look if he was up to date with his immunisations so I knew if he was covered for his tetanus vaccine, she told me I would have to wait 2 weeks for a nurse to action this. Here are only 2 examples of how unsafe it is for this woman to work on reception. She makes clinical decisions which I would deem as unsafe and are not within her scope of practice, and overall is a very rude unpleasant person to communicate with. Other than the receptionist, waiting times for appointments are extremely long, the doctor is different every appointment which is unfortunate for patients with long term health problems, also the gp practice appears to no longer be offering blood tests, patients are having to go up to tameside hospital to have their bloods done which can be very time consuming. I have had an ongoing problems with my health since October, each doctor I have seen has given me a different opinion, and I feel I am no closer to a diagnosis. As far as I am aware the NHS is supposed to facilitate informed decision making and involving the patient in their own care something I feel this GP practice does very poorly. I have had to take a lot of time out of work to be treated at the walk in centre due to the lack of care given. I am now unfortunately considering moving GP practice which is a shame as I have been a patient for a long time along with my 3 children and a lot of other extended family members.

recent_reviews.author: Martin Smith
recent_reviews.text: The level of service provided is wholly unacceptable. It is unnecessarily difficult to obtain treatment for even the most straightforward medical issues. Reception staff appear intent on creating barriers rather than facilitating solutions, routinely deflecting requests by insisting patients complete PATCHS forms instead of offering practical assistance. Every enquiry or attempt to seek help is met with the same obstructive response: complete another PATCHS form. I am extremely frustrated with being forced to submit repeated forms, only to receive an inadequate outcome from a GP whom I am unable to speak with directly. When concerns are raised about the quality of care, reception simply reiterates the same dismissive instruction — submit yet another form. To make matters worse, PATCHS forms are not even accessible in the app after a certain time of day, further restricting access to care. This is an inefficient and poorly designed system, upheld by staff who appear disengaged and unhelpful. It gives the strong impression that administrative gatekeeping and cost control are being prioritised over patient care, leaving patients stressed, dissatisfied, and without the timely treatment they require for routine illnesses. Clearly I'm not the only one that's experiencing this poor, unacceptable service as the majority of reviews are of negative experiences and the star rating at the time of this review is less than 2 stars, which is shocking for a community medical practice. Really unacceptable.

recent_reviews.text: Useless practice. Don't bother! Never have face-to-face appointments available. They now think it is decent to only provide telephone appointments, even for things that don't make sense. After the telephone appointments if you want to do a follow-up in person, bad luck there is no availability. What kind of GP is this? Besides why even bother pretending to have online service if it never has available appointments? ALL the time. Not everyone wants to call and stand in queues constantly. What's worse is they require you to call at exactly 8:00 am, which I have been trying, but apart from the retired, no one has time to do this. After many years this process hasn't improved. What really is the justification for continuing to use this method? The technology is available, there is an online service, so make use of it. The purpose of the GPs is to provide care to the residents. Thus having available appointments, otherwise for urgent care we have hospitals. If that isn't happening, it defeats the purpose of your existence. These people need to live up with the times, or close up!

recent_reviews.author: Mike Graham
recent_reviews.text: If I could post minus scores they would certainly get a minus score. I have a serious condition which is causing me excruciating pain. 9 weeks ago I had an appointment with a doctor from this clinic. He promised me that a letter would be sent to the hospital so I could have some scans. Due to no correspondence coming from this surgery other than to fill out surveys from Surveymonkey, I have to call repeatedly. Most times nobody will answer the phone. After no letter being sent I requested an emergency appointment and complained. As soon as I complained I was given an emergency face to face appointment. The doctor and receptionist apologized unreservedly and admitted my care was poor at this clinic. They promised me the letter would be sent as priority that day . Almost two weeks later after another 5 calls to the clinic I am told that the letter still hasn't been sent. Doctor has given me no pain relief and does not know anything about my condition. I cannot go to the hospital as I need a referral from a GP. We wonder why the NHS is in a poor state and underfunded and then look at this clinic and you see your answer. They do not care for you correctly. They allow your condition to deteriorate and do not make the correct referrals to the hospital at the right time . This means that the cost of your care increases massively and the length of time you suffer and the time it takes for you to get well again increases which in turn shortens your life span. They ignore the telephone. The receptionists are rude . They get prescriptions wrong all the time and seems like they alter your prescription without authorisation. The doctors seem to lack knowledge and common sense. The clinic is constantly empty but there are doctors and nurses there and yet they can never give you an appointment. The NHS need to do something regarding this type of doctor service. DO NOT USE THIS CLINIC.

recent_reviews.author: Sylvia Chan
recent_reviews.text: I seriously question the purpose of having a GP like this. Every single time I try to see a doctor, it is extremely, extremely, extremely difficult to get an appointment. In the past, they allowed walk-in appointments before 8 a.m., but this was later cancelled. Phone appointments were also available before, and then cancelled as well. They introduced a so-called “new system”, which I tried to use by filling in all the required information, only to be told that it was not possible and that I should make an online phone request instead. When I called the GP surgery again, I was told that this system is only open between 7 a.m. and 11 a.m. As a result, my illness was delayed for over a month and a half, and up to now I still cannot access my GP properly. I even went to other GP practices, but they simply referred me back to my local GP, which is this one. Thinking back on my past experiences, I honestly cannot recall a single time when I successfully booked an appointment and saw a doctor smoothly. On my very first appointment, I clearly booked a face-to-face consultation, but it was changed to a phone consultation without my consent. Because I was at work and missed the call, my appointment was immediately cancelled. When I later went to the surgery in person, I was told that my appointment could not be found in their system at all. I genuinely do not understand whether this GP surgery is functioning properly on a daily basis. In my opinion, the management and organisation are highly unprofessional and incompetent. Additionally, during a previous consultation, I explained to the doctor that I suspected two possible conditions. I then saw the doctor searching for symptoms on Google during the appointment. This made me seriously question the level of professionalism and medical competence. Overall, this has been a deeply frustrating and disappointing experience.

In the past, they allowed walk-in appointments before 8 a.m., but this was later cancelled. Phone appointments were also available before, and then cancelled as well. They introduced a so-called “new system”, which I tried to use by filling in all the required information, only to be told that it was not possible and that I should make an online phone request instead. When I called the GP surgery again, I was told that this system is only open between 7 a.m. and 11 a.m. As a result, my illness was delayed for over a month and a half, and up to now I still cannot access my GP properly. I even went to other GP practices, but they simply referred me back to my local GP, which is this one. Thinking back on my past experiences, I honestly cannot recall a single time when I successfully booked an appointment and saw a doctor smoothly. On my very first appointment, I clearly booked a face-to-face consultation, but it was changed to a phone consultation without my consent. Because I was at work and missed the call, my appointment was immediately cancelled. When I later went to the surgery in person, I was told that my appointment could not be found in their system at all. I genuinely do not understand whether this GP surgery is functioning properly on a daily basis. In my opinion, the management and organisation are highly unprofessional and incompetent. Additionally, during a previous consultation, I explained to the doctor that I suspected two possible conditions. I then saw the doctor searching for symptoms on Google during the appointment. This made me seriously question the level of professionalism and medical competence. Overall, this has been a deeply frustrating and disappointing experience.Like Share

recent_reviews.author: Azima Begum
recent_reviews.text: Absolutely disgusted at how bad Lindley have gotten over the last 3 years especially since they reduced priority appointments for babies from 5 apps to 1 a day. When they first opened on a temporary agreement they were brilliant even did weekend appointments. Once they received the patients votes to continue running surgery on a permanent basis they scrapped weekend appointments and just went downhill from there. Since the pandemic happened its almost impossible to get face to face for my young baby too, it takes 3 to 4 days of phoning at 8am to even get a phone appointment. After 3 telephone appointments for my under 1 year old In the last 3 weeks I asked for a face to face app today because my baby is not getting better.GP said I can bring baby in within an hour, I tried to explain I need alittle longer but GP didn’t care to hear it she insisted I attend within the hour or baby won’t be seen so I agreed. So when I finally did get a face to face appointment there was 0 flexibility offered which is not good when have other children to get to school. I must say the GP’s and reception staff in general are lovely and GP’s used to be really thorough when seen face to face, but that is unfortunately not the case anymore and the telephone appointments with the GP’s are just pointless and rushed. I will be changing GP, I know the pandemic has put an added pressure on NHS but I can honestly say after 3 years of going from bad to worse Lindley have no excuse for their lack of care & appointments for patients especially the vulnerable elderley patients and young children. I do believe Lindley can return to a really good practice like they once were if patient feedback is taken on board and they actually make changes and manage the practice properly.

recent_reviews.author: Lauren Fisher
recent_reviews.text: I feel this practice is the best example of why the NHS is so stretched and patients have to wait so long for an appointments. They don't seem to follow a good system therefore so many appointments are getting wasted and putting unnecessary pressure on the NHS. I was unable to get an appointment and due to my symptoms was advised to go A&E who done tests and referred me back to my GP for 2 further tests, which were clearly requested on the form so should have been able to book in directly with the nurse for these. The practice couldn't do this, said i needed a routine app with the gp to decide (5 weeks wait) then be referred back to the nurse (within the next 7 days - so 6 weeks minimum). I couldn't wait this long with lower body numbness so visited the walk in (2nd app in NHS) referred for bloods as A&E had advised. I attended the bloods appointment (3rd appointment in NHS) where they were unable to take said bloods which had now been documented as required twice. I was then advised i needed to see another GP to be referred back to the nurse - if I had stayed with this practice that would be 5 appointments, 5 mornings off work (self employed dental therapist so cancelling NHS patients of my own). I registered at a practice on Tuesday and have had my new patient check and the bloods that were requested by A&E within 2 days. Thee nurse at my new practice read the discharge note from A&E and done bloods as it was clearly stated by the Doctor that it was required. Please look into the way you run your practice, I totally understand practice protocols as i have managed a dental practice myself and worked in a GP surgery. The way you operate is ineffective and is straining the NHS therefore inconveniencing your patients. On a positive note i feel all the staff i have met in the short time at the practice have been very nice, pleasent and do try to help there just bound by the lack of appointments of protocols they have to follow

recent_reviews.author: Angela
recent_reviews.text: Doctors are great! However, even though you constantly ring from surgery opening, it is not guaranteed you'll get through! Then when you eventually get answered an hour later, appointments have all gone! Doesn't matter that you're ill, you can't have one, until next week or wait to go through same process all again over again! The old system was so much better! 4 years on from this review, the surgery has become, not fit for service. I received a text, to make urgent appointment, so I ring, and no appointments available. Ring following morning, as soon as phone lines open, and told I'm 20th in the queue to speak to receptionist. Yeah, right! Not only, have I waited for 2 months for results, I can't get an appointment. I was told at one point, they were delayed, and they would only contact me, if they showed something. I have no faith in any of them, anymore! Even the consultants at the hospital, roll their eyes, at the mention of this surgery, now! It used to be, one of the best. Now it is probably the worst. An update 24th March 2025. Gordon street medical centre is now, no longer taking appointments over the phone or over the reception desk. Told to access on line, by text, with no clear instructions on how? I'm certain there'll be unnecessary deaths, through this total lack of care, and receptionist has put the phone down on me, just for asking her name. My husband has physically approached reception, and has come home with zero help. I will be making official complaint!

recent_reviews.author: Mark Cole
recent_reviews.text: Good afternoon I would like to give you some feedback on my experience, but I would like to do this in a respectful, fair-minded way. I hope you take it in the spirit in which it is offered. I am a long-standing blood donor. I was unable to donate at my last appointment. because of a low Iron level. Their protocol determined I should have a follow up blood test at my GP. I attempted to book this at the practice but was told it would need to be authorised by the GP, this is understandable. I attempted to do this through PATCHS. The first two days this was not possible as there was no capacity in the system. This was the same on the third day, but then at 12.00 midday I managed to access then system. Not sure when it clears? I assumed the beginning of the day? PATCHS was then excellent, and a blood test authorised within the hour. But attempting to make the appointment was more problematic. 3 days, about 10 attempts, different times of day, on the phone for a total of around 3 hours could not get through. Some of these the automated service said I was first in the que. Based on how long I was waiting I have some doubts about this. In the end I walked to the surgery and made the appointment face to face. There were two receptionists, not unpleasant, but quite “minimalist” in their interactions, empty waiting room, they were not do anything that would have prevented them from answering a phone. Not sure if these are people responsible for incoming calls? Appointment was made, the earliest available was 18 working days. I guess I am lucky it was routine. Having worked in public service, including healthcare for 50 years I do appreciate there are often hidden complexities that the public may not see. But overall impression. Some parts of the system seem to work and some not. Could the donation centre have taken my blood? PATCHS works well when you can access it. Incredibly hard to get through to the GP. Long appointment wait for something that feels very routine and quick to do. When I am seen, based on previous experience I every confidence that it will be efficient and the staff respectful. But it feels it is harder than it should be and with some concentrated thought some opportunities for quick wins here.

recent_reviews.author: Terry D
recent_reviews.text: Update: 15/04/25 I am updating regarding the new PATCHS to arrange medical care. So today I login 7.30 and fill the form in, severe pain in my elbow, I do not receive a call or appointment instead I get SMS to say the Doctor wants you to see a Physio but sorry no appointments, So no diagnosis and no care, how can a Doctor refer you to a department without a diagnosis ? It appears to me this new system is now being used to clear any backlogs but you do not receive any care, My request is now showing on the system as completed but I have no idea what is wrong or what I should do, It is disgusting, the practice looks good on the system as they have cleared the daily requests, I wonder how many other people got this type of care. My only option now is to go to A+E, I am 60 and have never used A+E unless I was seriously in need to go, I have even refused Ambulances to take me because I feel A+E is busy enough. What a great way to pass your work load over. Unfortunately this GP service no longer has a GP, my last two appointments have not been a Doctor even though I requested a Doctor, today trying to make an appointment I am being told some one who is not a Doctor is just as good as a Doctor, some how I do not think so and I do not feel they should be telling patients this either. Becoming a GP in the UK takes 9-11 years. One appointment the lady I had to see, phoned a friend while I was sitting there to get advise on how to proceed, not a very good experience, then she explained she could not issue the medication I required and would need to speak with the GP, the GP I wanted to speak to.

It appears to me this new system is now being used to clear any backlogs but you do not receive any care, My request is now showing on the system as completed but I have no idea what is wrong or what I should do, It is disgusting, the practice looks good on the system as they have cleared the daily requests, I wonder how many other people got this type of care. My only option now is to go to A+E, I am 60 and have never used A+E unless I was seriously in need to go, I have even refused Ambulances to take me because I feel A+E is busy enough. What a great way to pass your work load over. Unfortunately this GP service no longer has a GP, my last two appointments have not been a Doctor even though I requested a Doctor, today trying to make an appointment I am being told some one who is not a Doctor is just as good as a Doctor, some how I do not think so and I do not feel they should be telling patients this either. Becoming a GP in the UK takes 9-11 years. One appointment the lady I had to see, phoned a friend while I was sitting there to get advise on how to proceed, not a very good experience, then she explained she could not issue the medication I required and would need to speak with the GP, the GP I wanted to speak to.Like5 Share Response from the owner 11 months agoThank you for your feedback. recent_reviews.text: If you value your life do not use these doctors. Total lack of care. I’m a new patient. I have been without my prescription and put in a request. I will be switching gps again as I can’t stomach the idea of having to fight for a doctor or staff to do their job and not expect me to do their admin work for them while at the same time suggesting I’m unfit to relay my previous prescription needs. recent_reviews.text: Referred here after I refused to go A&E and the ACU nurse had concerns as I have COVID, CEV and chest pain. Stated that my chest is totally clear and I'm perfectly fine. Such a contrast to the 111 Doctors and Nurses I spoke to; its always best to over-care than under-care. My health conditions are lifelong and individuals like this are the ones who make me lose confidence and put my life at risk as I can't trust them to have 1% of humanity or at least fulfil their DUTY. I should have opted for gotodoc at Wythenshawe.

recent_reviews.author: Rebecca Berg
recent_reviews.text: No-one ever seems to write positive comments. When service is good few people ever review so I want to share my experience. I have had nothing but great service from this GP practise. Although sometimes there is a queue on the phone (the old phone system used to just hang up whilst waiting) they have a new phone system that gives you a queue number so you know roughly how long the wait will be. The receptionists, practise nurse and doctors have been nothing but professional each and every time I have visited them. The receptionists have always been so helpful chasing repeat prescriptions, test results etc. When the walk in centre was here it was manic due to countless people waiting but as this has now moved to the hospital it is much calmer. I want to say thank you to all of the staff here, you do an amazing job in difficult circumstances. The NHS is a wonderful thing and people should remember the receptionists doctors and nurses are people too - don't take your frustrations out on them they are human and deserve to be treated as such.

recent_reviews.author: David Duncan
recent_reviews.text: Good facilities, physiotherapist and pharmacy on site. Parking just outside the front. I have attended the centre on numerous occasions for different reasons and so has my partner. She was prescribed the birth control pill over the phone even though late for her period. Thankfully she took a pregnancy test herself, we are expecting a child. We reported the Dr. I have to collect a repeat prescription for myself every 4 weeks for nearly a year now and only once has it been correct and ready for collection. Whilst I have nothing but respect and admiration for the NHS and all of it's staff for the hard work they do for the community. I do feel that the left hand isn't always talking to it's right hand when visting this primary care centre. There are some outstanding staff who work here that are unfortunately over shadowed by the obvious mis-communication. Trying to get through on the phone to reception is a long drawn out process. I guess there are limited resources in this area.

recent_reviews.author: Nicole K
recent_reviews.text: It was suggested to me in my very own private appointment with test results & support that my son may need some further help years ahead as he was too young to be diagnosed at the time or have a referral made, so I then asked his primary school for the extra help with also a false accusation made against me to the authorities, this is becoming like an obsessed safeguarding problem full of inappropriate questions for single parents that only want the best for their children to succeed in education, I would of appreciated some help with this, also I don't think it's fair on undiagnosed but suspected earlier on that children should be made to go to the walk in with anxieties/refusals due to NO discipline or help in these schools that do not support or deal with bullying fairly, making it difficult for me again, then I have to make an appeal to change her enviroment so she feels safe in her surroundings & I reckon they should be allowed to see a nurse or GP ASAP!!! with any self harming issues that are discussed, bringing the parent into this & making them feel like they are the problem is nothing but stressful when they have enough on their plate to attend with- more refusals, no diagnosis or written plans. So please improve on children's referrals & appointments it's not too much to request, it should just be a speedy check up not a rejected one then accused of not taking my child for help being pressured by 4 people that know nothing about child abuse, quite racist actually when she is naturally fair with dark hair & can't get into a decent sleeping routine or leave the house without me, it's not always appearances all the damage is recorded in the information & should of been passed on to Early Years meeting as they thought I just leave her with no help, I've been requesting help from you for years then the replies are go to the school with these questions how can that be done when they all put safeguarding above everything else, as a child i was severely neglected & abused, I know exaclty what it looks like & others should know aswell how it appears from the outside, so this is one big joke & hopefully, one day the supported well cared for children get all the help they need to manage well through life, things need changing, parent blaming is nothing but delaying & unfair.

recent_reviews.text: This by far is the worse GP Surgery I and my family have ever experienced…where do I start from? My daughter is 16 weeks old meanwhile this GP Surgery has on 2 occasions cancelled her 12 weeks immunisation appointment on the last minute… I’ve today asked for a referral elsewhere nearby but the receptionist said her manager said it can only be done there. From the way things are going, my daughter might have her 12 weeks immunisation at 1 year old with this GP Surgery. My daughter again has got skin rashes which we had an appointment and prescribed creams late November but the creams are not working, I rang in to request an appointment to see the GP, the receptionist asked me to hold on so she can speak to the doctor about it, the next minute the receptionist says GP has sent the same cream that’s not working to the pharmacy, I collected the cream, applied as prescribed but it’s still not working, I rang in for an appointment on Monday and was told GP rang in sick and that we should take my daughter to the walk-in center at Tameside Hospital. As for myself, I have a pregnant woman’s full details wrongly sent to me including , consultation history an anti sickness prescription sat on my patchs account for weeks even after I had rang the reception to complain about it and request for this information to be deleted. Where lies the confidentiality of clients information? My wife hasn’t been left out of their poor service, she had an episiotomy during childbirth in September 2025 and was stitched which resulted to an overgranulation, we’ve complained about it to the GP, she was seen my the midwife 2 weeks ago who said she was going to refer my wife to the Gynaecologist and as of now, no referral, no update! I honestly miss my former GP Surgery - High Lane Medical Practice

recent_reviews.text: I’ve been a patient at this practice for over 15 years and have always been treated well in the past — but the sleep group has gone completely downhill. I’ve been dealing with the same issue for over 3 years, and nothing has ever been resolved. The appointment system is useless — it constantly sends me to the wrong department, and nobody seems able or willing to fix it. I’ve spoken with Charlotte and Annette, who were both unhelpful, dismissive, and showed no interest in actually sorting things out. Their attitude was rude and unprofessional — something I’ve never experienced here before. To make things worse, the receptionists have no manners whatsoever and seem to think they’re doctors. The lack of basic courtesy and professionalism is shocking, especially after so many years of being a loyal patient. It’s extremely disappointing to see how far the standards have dropped. Management seriously needs to address these issues — both with the staff’s attitude and the broken appointment system.

recent_reviews.author: M. Jones
recent_reviews.text: One gp here was nice because he listened to me when I had problems with my mental health. But the other GP (the arrogant and overpowering one) just re-traumatised me when they made me talk through a horrific assault I'd experienced in another healthcare building from a professional. At the time I should have said no to talking through this trauma, but at this time I was so weak because of the PTSD I wasn't putting my own wellbeing first. I got copies of my medical records years later and discovered that this GP didn't type into my records the details of the trauma I had told them of. So that GP had me talking through this trauma (which worsened my mental health and exhausted me) for nothing. Also , it meant that there was less evidence in my medical records. (I was traumatised for years, the NHS minimised this trauma, so did GMC, and I reported too but they failed to act. You're not safe anywhere, and supposedly safe buildings are ideal for predators to work in. Avoid going into appointments on your own if you need something doing. I can't go near most of them now for fear, and many talk down to us anyway while dismissing patients.) This GP also likes to pressure patients ignoring the fact they are fragile, and is the competitive type. Astonishing that they don't understand PTSD and that you can easily worsen the patient's mental health if you are verbally thoughtless. Another thing about this surgery is that the GP's here are not very knowledgeable... I was going in to this surgery coughing non-stop, and they didn't even explore what could have been causing my cough. Well over two years later an open minded respiratory consultant sent me to ENT and we finally discovered that I'd been suffering from LPR for over 2 years. This type of reflux isn't very rare and I'm still shocked that the GP's here didn't even think of this. They would just type "coughing day and night" consistently into my records each time I went into this surgery, and I'd then go home after making no progress. At least I stopped buying useless pills they kept pushing me to buy. Aloe Vera juice worked much better to relieve my symptoms. I'm glad I refused pills for anxiety and depression - they are very bad for the body. Sometimes all doctors do is destroy us.

recent_reviews.author: Ken Kamdy
recent_reviews.text: A call was initiated to ascertain why an appointment for a mother and child was declined by a GP, providing clinical advice to the service user, and you are not part of the medical team. NHS staff must not unreasonably deny access to services, and patients are entitled to be treated with dignity, receive clear information, and file a formal complaint regarding inadequate care or discourteous conduct. However, a staff member and a receptionist unjustly canceled an appointment, and I have requested the call log. Non-clinical reception staff should not act as if they are GPs; clinical decisions regarding whether a baby or parent requires a review should be made by a qualified health professional (GP, nurse, ANP) following appropriate triage protocols. Professional guidance underscores that healthcare professionals must not unreasonably refuse a patient access to care that addresses their needs and must communicate with kindness and clarity, particularly with vulnerable patients such as parents of very young children. A receptionist informing a practice or service user that she does not consult a GP also provides clinical advice to the service user. Merely asserting that a one-year-old “does not need to see a GP” without a proper clinical evaluation or justification is unlikely to adhere to good practice standards regarding communication and access to care. It is unfortunate that this matter is not being addressed; I intend to escalate this issue further due to the appalling service.

Non-clinical reception staff should not act as if they are GPs; clinical decisions regarding whether a baby or parent requires a review should be made by a qualified health professional (GP, nurse, ANP) following appropriate triage protocols. Professional guidance underscores that healthcare professionals must not unreasonably refuse a patient access to care that addresses their needs and must communicate with kindness and clarity, particularly with vulnerable patients such as parents of very young children. A receptionist informing a practice or service user that she does not consult a GP also provides clinical advice to the service user. Merely asserting that a one-year-old “does not need to see a GP” without a proper clinical evaluation or justification is unlikely to adhere to good practice standards regarding communication and access to care. recent_reviews.author: Fiona Simpson
recent_reviews.text: I am always really happy with and satisfied with all interactions with the surgery, and actually recommend it to others. The 2 main doctors and advanced clinician are always very good and are through, listen and take concerns seriously. The patches system is very good and easy to use - myself and spouse have had to use it a few times recently, and we have always then been contacted with an appropriate appointment, if that was face to face, urgent phone, or routine that has always happened quickly. There are some people complaining about lack of appointments etc, I have never found this to be the case. I work in primary care and regularly deal with different GP surgeries, and believe me, simpson medical are one of the better ones!! Perhaps everyone needs to have realistic expectations, and consider that there is high demand for healthcare, which exceeds capacity. The old days of face to face appointments are gone, unless it is necessary this does not happen anymore - often phone calls, including photos etc are often sufficent, and more a more efficient use of staff resources. If a face to face appointment is necessary it will be made whilst anything regarding mental health has always been taking seriously and urgently. I am very happy with being a patient here, and think given the demand they do a good job, and are one of the better surgeries I deal with. Thank you to the staff, I appreciate it

recent_reviews.text: Giving this place even just one star hurts to be honest. Had an appointment at 12.20, arrived at 12.15. Not seen until 13.30!!!! They also took 4 weeks to give me my blood test results. After my blood test on 6th October I waited 2 weeks for them to contact me with my results. I called them - they told me to ring another number. That number told me to ring these guys back. Turns out they had my results all along. Waited another 2 weeks for an appointment for my results, only for the doctor to call for said appointment and tell me they have no results for me. I call back to the reception desk and get told by a lady on reception that someone didn’t download my results off an email. Another appointment booked for my results. Waited til the next week to get my results finally. They are a joke operation - if you value your health, go elsewhere. It is THAT simple! Whilst I sat waiting for my appointment, 2 other patients were kicking off over medical negligence claims. I’m not surprised!!!!

recent_reviews.author: Javaria Afzal
recent_reviews.text: If I could give minus 10 stars I would. Absolute joke of a medical practise. My husband had an appointment on Monday at 2:45pm, 5 minutes before the appointment the receptionist loudly starts laughing and saying Rizwan (the doctor we’re meant to be seeing in 5 minutes) isn’t in today he told me on Friday that he’s not in. They begin to loudly start trying to locate the doctor saying he never told anyone that he’s not going to be in and that he has appointments. They ring him and surpise surpise he’s not in, even though they 1- gave us the appointment with him, 2- rang at 1pm to confirm that it’s with him and 3- didn’t realise until 5 minutes before the appointment that he’s not even in. They then tell us sorry your appointments cancelled come back tomorrow. My husband has a foot infection and is already in pain, was hard enough to come the first time never mind coming again. Anyways we get an appointment the next day, the dr was good and took her time to check it thoroughly, spoke to other doctors took a swab and prescribed antibiotics. She even called back a few hours later and gave more advice. Can’t fault her at all, it’s the receptionists that give this place a bad name. The dr was told by someone whilst we were there to not send prescriptions to wise pharmacy as it’s closed due to the police blocking off the road. So she sends the prescription to Manchester pharmacy instead. We get to Manchester pharmacy and it’s also closed so we ring the gp back to let them know, the receptionist just says oh wait for tomorrow, not considering infections get worse without treatment, we tell her we need the antibiotics she says try a different pharmacy. We go to Asda pharmacy and they say ur gp needs to cancel it first then we can dispense. Rang gp AGAIN she just says oh no we can’t cancel it. We end up going to another pharmacy and they call the surgery themselves and got it cancelled. It took us 4 hours of running around just to get some antibiotics, absolute joke.

recent_reviews.author: Paulette Crawford King
recent_reviews.text: Where do I start with this place. Anyway I put in a repeated prescription on line on a Monday, went to pick it up from the pharmacy on the Thursday (Bearing in mind it should take 2 days to receive). I got to the Pharmacy only for them to tell me that this Medical center didn't send over the prescription. I called the so called Medical Center to see why my prescription was not processed. After a long time trying to get through to the receptionist I had to repeat my DOB nearly 6 times. I asked why they never sent my prescription over and she said it's because I need a review but she will get the Doctor to ring me back. The Doctor rang back and we made arrangements for me to get my prescription the following morning. To cut a long story short, l went back to the Pharmacy the following afternoon and my prescription was still not there. Again I rang the surgery and not one person could tell me what was going on. I now put it down to a language barrier within that surgery. They need to have staff that speak the same language like the minority of patients like myself who only speak English. I really don't know where to go with this because they only look after their own. I say this because last year I put in a complaint about one of their absolutely rude nurse and was told that someone will call me try and resolve the complaint I put in. I am still waiting for that person to call me back until today. I have no confidence in this place and I feel it is because I am a minority within that surgery. I must also make it clear that this has been my surgery for over 30 years and since the previous owners left, the place as gone completely disgusting. All I ask is that they treat everyone the same,we are all human beings. Trust me I am going to take this further, hopefully I can get someone who speaks English like I do. 😡😡

recent_reviews.author: Muoi N
recent_reviews.text: Honestly not sure why they haven’t made any changes even with all the bad reviews. So tired of this practice. I book a telephone appointment and up until the day of this appointment I receive multiple text reminders that my appointment is at 1pm. I wait and receive no call, I then have to call them and ask why they haven’t called me - their response is that they called me early morning so I missed my appointment, have to book again and that I should have ignored the messages I got from the practice telling me it was at 1pm? Why are you sending out these appointment times and not sticking to them? Ordering prescriptions is also a pain. I come in to order a prescription, they say I have to do it online. I order them online and they confirm it, a week later I’m still not able to get the prescription so I called them and they said they never did it!! I then order over the phone for my parents which was fine, two days later I try ordering for myself and they said they aren’t allowed to take it over the phone and that I have to come in?! Asked them why I was allowed to do it over the phone two days ago...they said "don’t know, that person shouldn’t have done that for you" Although I’m sure I spoke to the same woman. What’s with the inconsistencies? Such bad service, it’s actually unbelievable.

recent_reviews.author: Rehab Sherif
recent_reviews.text: I had an extremely disappointing experience with this dentist. My appointment was 25 minutes long and I arrived 7 minutes late, due to the car park being full, having to find and pay for on-street parking, and arranging (and paying for) a babysitter to attend the appointment. I explained the situation clearly to the receptionist and asked for it to be relayed to the dentist. Despite this, the dentist showed no empathy or flexibility. After waiting six years to finally register with an NHS dentist since moving to Manchester, I was shocked to be told I would be taken off the register for being late once — something that, having worked in two dental practices myself, I have never known to be standard policy. What made the situation worse was the dentist’s behaviour: instead of speaking to me directly like a professional, he avoided the conversation entirely and hid behind a wall, while incorrectly claiming I was “over 10 minutes late.” This felt dismissive, unprofessional, and frankly inhumane. After such a long wait to access NHS dental care, this experience was incredibly upsetting. Patients deserve understanding, honesty, and basic respect — none of which were shown here.

recent_reviews.author: Junaid Ahmed
recent_reviews.text: As a long-term patient (diagnosed with a life time illness since 2005) receiving continuous prescriptions and specialized care, I requested a paid private letter confirming the simple, medically accepted fact that chronic stress and hardship trigger flare-ups to my condition. The practice refused the request, claiming "insufficient evidence" a shocking statement considering my two decades as a patient for whom they have continuously prescribed, medication, are informed of my hospital ongoing treatment for years (Vedolizumab, etc.) and liaised with the hospital IBD team. This refusal demonstrates a failure to understand the patient they are treating. Crucially, this contradiction occurred even though I attached an older letter from my specialist consultant where this clinical fact was already written and acknowledged. This extreme administrative obstacle wasted significant time and energy, forcing me to change GPs due to their unwillingness to support a chronic patient.

recent_reviews.author: JUNAID AHMED
recent_reviews.text: I was a long-term patient with multiple chronic conditions, including ulcerative colitis, arthritis, and migraines — all of which were regularly managed through prescriptions and hospital treatments. I requested a simple private letter confirming my diagnosis and how stress can affect my condition — something a hospital consultant had previously provided. Despite being willing to pay the £35 fee, the practice refused to provide the letter and didn’t offer an appointment to discuss it. As someone managing serious long-term health issues, I found this response dismissive and lacking in basic patient support. I’ve since moved to a new GP who I hope will be more patient-focused. I’m sharing this to help others understand what kind of support they might — or might not — receive here if they have complex or ongoing health needs. To the management: the decline in care became noticeable after COVID. If you’re genuinely reviewing patient experiences, it may be worth examining the internal changes made during and after the pandemic — because that’s when the ship started sinking.

Their monitoring of my health conditions (annual health checks) have always been prompt. I feel fortunate to be a registered patient at this practice.

recent_reviews.author: Saqib Javed
recent_reviews.text: I am having a horrible experience with this surgery for some time now. In order to get a simple blood test done, I had two appointments cancelled by the surgery with a text message sent a couple of hours before the appointments citing staff absences/shortages. Finally, the test went ahead on the third occasion. On another occasion my 7 year old son was given appointment almost a month after I rang them to get a simple blood test. Finally, on the day of his appointment we were just 2 min late and the receptionists turned us away saying you are late and the nurse is very busy today. I asked her to speak to the nurse and she refused to do so saying "I know her answer already she wont see you". I am registered with this surgery for more than 10 years and never in my experience I was seen on time. The surgery is always running between 10 to 30 mins late into each appointment and the patients are supposed to wait until finally seen by someone. This is not fair on patients as the surgery expects them to wait for the doctor or the nurse when they are running late whereas if the patient is one minute late they don't bother to see us even if we are willing to wait. I don't see the logic in it. If I am two minutes late with a child that means someone else must be seen during my time slot then why can't I wait and be seen in the slot of the patient who is seen before his/her appointment. Technically speaking, from the 10 mins slot allocated to me I still had 8 minutes remaining and I know the blood tests only take 5 mins.

recent_reviews.author: Ian Dobbin
recent_reviews.text: This surgery has been deteriorating rapidly over recent years. I have been registered for over 30 years and used to have confidence in the service offered. However, their main aim now appears to be to bat off patients as soon as possible. This is illustrated by my recent contact when I missed a call from a GP by seconds. He then re-dialled within 30 seconds (while I was attempting to contact the surgery) thereby disqualifying me from an appointment that day due to 2 missed calls. I must now wait 3 days until Monday to try again. When I contacted the surgery the receptionist was insensitive bordering on rude. This is not the first time I have experienced this response from this surgery. While I have a lot of sympathy with the pressure the NHS is under, there is no excuse for this sort of treatment of patients.

recent_reviews.author: Mia Smith
recent_reviews.text: Some really nice staff but on the whole this is the most incompetent and negligent GP practice's I have ever been to. They messed up my registration which they did admit fault and apologies for but it caused me to miss 2 weeks of prescription. Got a call back to book a blood test- get to the day of my appointment it was never put into the system. Got the blood test at a later date but get very conflicting information about the results. -Used the online system to requested a GP appointment regarding blood test- I get an email saying literally just "your results are normal" and no offer of appointment. When I rung up to get some detail I found out some things couldn't be tested because the sample spoiled and they want a retest- that's fair enough it happens- but there was no mention of that on the email. Most importantly found out they didn't test what the GP told me the test was for- wouldn't have found this out if I hadn't rung. The online system is hit and miss, sometimes very helpful, other times the responses are unhelpful, vague and do not answer the question. Can normally get an appointment on your 1st or 2nd attempt which is pretty good given how many people they must service, and some of the GPs have been good, others less so but that's always the way. Decent enough for medication reviews but if you want help for any new issues would not recommend. You have to be constantly on it else you will slip through the cracks.

recent_reviews.author: Νεφέλη Πάσχου
recent_reviews.text: Extremely uncaring reception staff - aside from frequently experiencing issues with them being full (even if forms are filled in the morning), if you receive a phone call that you cannot take right then, chances are that you will miss your appointment entirely. The "doctors will call back" response I have received from reception if I call them directly is often a lie as well, as I have had to personally ring them back again due to not receiving a call back. I appreciate that the demand might be high and something might get overlooked, but giving misleading expectations should not be acceptable, and should at least be met with an apology when it happens. An example of missing an appointment was when I was in the toilet (due to the pain I was experiencing from my issue), called back within 10 mins, and was met with a rude response and no alternative, just a "try again tomorrow". I almost always receive calls after 5pm no matter how early I fill in the form as well, which as you can imagine, makes scheduling hell and it is extremely difficult to ever be seen. It's at the very least disappointing to experience no sympathy or understanding from staff. Effort to help patients/introduce alternative appointment methods should be higher, especially since the form system clearly has tons of issues, and reliance on GP services is very high right now.

recent_reviews.text: Worst surgery ever! I dont even know where to begin. Needed urgent blood test done of my children. After 13 cancellations and 2 times they lost the blood sample we finally got the result and the doctor wanted to repeat the test. It took us 6 months to get all the test done because apparently they only have one paediatric nurse who is off sick all the time! We complained last time and they just blamed NHS for lack of funding. We got an apology at the end. Gave them a call again last month as my child been unwell again and the doctor told us to get a immediate blood test done. We are still waiting for an appointment. I spoke to the doctor on 29th June and they already cancelled couple of appointments on the day couple of hours before the appointment. We took time of work on many occasions but they just cancel the appointment last minute. I am just so fed up of dealing with them that I havent been to GP in years. Obviously I have to take my children in when they are unwell and then I have to deal with all this. I have been really unwell and filled in a form this week where I clearly stated I am having occasional chest pain and difficulty breathing for last few weeks along with other things. Well got a call back and the doctor spoke to me about one symptoms I am not too worried about and booked in a blood test next week for it. I told her about the chest pain again and she said she will see me after the blood test and talk about this!!! I've decided to go A&E as these doctors clearly dont know what they are doing! Avoid like plague! This place is abolute chaos.

recent_reviews.author: Naya Rehman
recent_reviews.text: My mother has been a patient at this practise for years now. She has learning difficulties and suffers with mental health problems. She has had ADHD assessments and additional tests done to find out what her diagnosis was, she was told to hand in this paper work to the reception at the practise (before covid) they misplaced all these documents with all her initial assessments and results in there. Since then she has been on several different medications unsure of what it is actually tackling, she has gained weight due to the medication she’s been given. Her doctors have given her numerous numbers to call to redo them assessments and figure out on her own what she has - which she is still on waiting lists for. She doesn’t get a face to face review with her doctor regularly, only last year a mental health nurse rang her up, as it got extreme, however she’s been suffering with severe mental health her entire life. I’m 20 years old and struggle with my own mental health as I have been supporting my mother my entire life and have been on the other end of her episodes which she hasn’t received the right/enough support for. Wouldn’t recommend this practise especially if your suffering with mental health as it isn’t as prioritised.

recent_reviews.author: Romi Morris
recent_reviews.text: Indeed ! One of worst gp surgery in the country. If you go up to 5 minutes you will have to book another appointment. However they can make you sit hours and hours for your appointment. In another words THEY ARE ALLOWED TO MAKE MISTAKES BUT YOU CAN'T.
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Romi MorrisLocal Guide · 23 reviews · 6 photos3 years ago Indeed ! One of worst gp surgery in the country. If you go up to 5 minutes you will have to book another appointment. However they can make you sit hours and hours for your appointment. In another words THEY ARE ALLOWED TO MAKE MISTAKES BUT YOU CAN'T.Like1 Share Response from the owner 3 years agoHello Romi. I'm sorry to hear that you feel we're the worst GP surgery in the country and that you're unhappy with the way we conduct appointments. Whilst we would like to give patients a long amount of time to discuss their issues, that is just not possible at the moment. This is because there has been a huge surge in demand for appointments since the pandemic, which has also been increased by the prevalence of winter illnesses that seem to be spreading around our community. However, we do allocate more than five minutes per appointment for each patient. Regarding waiting for hours for an appointment, I’m unsure if you’ve had a face-to-face appointment that you’ve been kept waiting for, or if you’re referring to a telephone consultation. I’ve not heard of patients having to wait for hours in the practice for an appointment but if that is the case please do let me know by filling in a feedback form on our website as that would be very concerning. If you’re talking about telephone consultations, we are unable to give exact time scales for telephone appointments as there are so many variables that may throw a specific appointment time off track. This could be an emergency appointment needing to be seen first, other patients not answering the doctors call, patients needing a bit of extra time to discuss their medical problems and more. When you book a telephone consultation, you should however be told to expect a call either in the morning or the afternoon. Kind Regards, Lauren, Engagement & Communications Officer

recent_reviews.author: Nellight
recent_reviews.text: The worst experience with any GP so far. It took them over 4 weeks to register me even though I already had an issue to deal with urgently. Then, the online form is broken and doesn't accept international phone numbers which makes it literally impossible to book an appointment through their website. I tried to call and after over 30 minutes in the queue three times I was either told to call back the next day or they simply hung up on me. They also have seem to forgotten my referral to a specialist which should have been done weeks ago. I am honestly just exhausted at this point.

I am honestly just exhausted at this point.Like3 Share Response from the owner 3 years agoHello Stickman. Thank you for your review. I'm sorry to hear that we've provided the worst experience you've had with a GP so far. We are located in the heart of popular Manchester student areas, and have received an unprecedented amount over registrations over September and October. Our team have been working very hard to get through these registrations, but the volume of registrations has meant that it has taken longer than we would have hoped to get patients onto our system. Thank you for pointing out the issue with international numbers and our online forms. We want every patient to be able to easily access healthcare so I will certainly get this looked into. We aren't able to control how many people are waiting in the telephone queue to get through to the reception team. Our reception staff members work very hard to get through the calls but if we have a lot of people calling, the queue can get very large. That is why we do encourage those who are able to use the online form system to do so. We are a same day only appointment service and it is ran on a first come first served basis (unless you require an emergency appointment). We aren't able to book appointments in advance and unfortunately, once the appointments for the day are booked, we aren't able to offer any more. I understand this can be really frustrating, but this means we are able to give patients the care they need when they need it and avoids patients having to wait for weeks at a time to speak to a doctor. Unfortunately, due to the public nature of this forum, I'm unable to comment on your referral or being hung up on. If you would like me to look into those issues for you, please do let me know by filling in a feedback form here: https://bit.ly/3fequhN Kind Regards, Lauren, Engagement & Communications Officer

recent_reviews.author: Eron Ameen
recent_reviews.text: This GP needs a lot of more improvements, when you want an appointment, they tell us do it online rather than book for us straight away over the phone, physical appointments almost don’t exist anymore! then the doctor rings us in unexpected time while we are busy.
recent_reviews.raw_card_text: Eron AmeenLocal Guide · 30 reviews3 years ago This GP needs a lot of more improvements, when you want an appointment, they tell us do it online rather than book for us straight away over the phone, physical appointments almost don’t exist anymore! then the doctor rings us in unexpected time while we are busy.Like2 Share Response from the owner 3 years agoHello Eron. Thank you for your review. We do encourage patients who are able to use the e-consult system to do so as this allows our reception team more time to help those patients who aren't able to use the internet. Our reception team also do not book appointments, they only request them - the same as when you submit an online form. A doctor or a nurse will then triage your request and decide what course of action is needed, whether that be a prescription, telephone consult or face to face appointment. Along with our e-consult system, we do also operate a telephone triage system. This means that all patients will be given a phone call first and if it's needed, will be invited into the surgery for a face to face appointment. We've found that telephone consultations have been really beneficial and have allowed patients to get the help they need from the comfort of their own home. We'll always try our best to call at a time that suits you but can't always guarantee this will happen as the demand for appointments is really high at the moment and we try and help as many people as we possibly can throughout the day. To make sure that patients do not miss their appointment, we also call twice throughout the day to reach you. If you aren't available at a certain point in the day, please make sure you let us know on your request so your doctor or nurse is clear on when they can and can't reach you. We do hope that in the future you will have a more positive experience with us here at The Robert Darbishire Practice. Kind Regards, Lauren, Engagement & Communications Officer

recent_reviews.author: Elspeth Woolsey
recent_reviews.text: Go elsewhere. I'm exhausted with this Practice. I have ignored quite a few things but will be looking elsewhere as they could raise your blood rather than help. I'm not a fan of their online system (but that's my preference) and after waiting over 20mins, was then told to explain my symptoms online. This is not the first time this type of response has happened and I'm sick of a doctors practice getting fixated on my autoimmune disease rather than the issue I've come with - I'm aware they could and can be related but it would be nice to have the issue investigated rather than just put under the umbrella of my auto-immune disease but she completely ignored me telling her ho my body had been feeling leading up the issue. I walked there during my lunch hour to be told they hadn't received it, went to the doctors and wait ed 5-10mins for the receptionist machine to load up before telling me it was at a different pharmacy!! (Again, not the first time they've done this this when I asked for it to be sent to this pharmacy!) The nurses are the best thing about this place but I'm fed up with the lack of care or interest from doctors - I'm aware of my body, so am also aware when something is not right. It might be good if you could listen to to your patients and go from there.

recent_reviews.author: X
recent_reviews.text: Using this practice almost makes it feel like you don't have a GP. It is completely unsuitable for anyone in work or study - to get any sort of appointment, you have to wait all day on a ringback from a doctor or nurse who wants a 10 second soundbite of your problem before deciding whether your issue is worthy enough to get an appointment. The receptionists refuse to give you a time for this ringback - it could be at any point during the day and if you miss it you've screwed. What if I am driving, at work, in a meeting, in the shower? Patients should not have to sit by their phones all day to receive basic medical care. On top of this, when you enter the waiting room it is crowded and often noisy and the staff are running late - I've sat there for 30 minutes on occassion and felt physically anxious as a result. Perhaps you could take on fewer patients (and make less money) but provide an accessible service so I feel like I can actually use the NHS? The only upside is that most of the staff I have encountered have been nice apart from a rude Nurse Practioner and GP.
