recent_reviews.author: L B
recent_reviews.text: GP's and Nurses are brilliant. Always friendly and easy to talk to. Both nurses I've seen there have been bubbly, happy and chatty and put me at ease, even when having a cervical screening :') One of the reception staff comes across very rude on the phone at times which isn't great when you're ringing up about mental health issues. She has at other times when I've physically been in the surgery been fantastic and extremely helpful. I can sympathise with them to an extent as they must get a lot of abuse but it shouldn't be pushed onto others. When you're physically in the building though they're all spot on. Struggle to get through and get appointments if you don't keep trying to ring at 08:00. They do seem to have introduced a phone queuing system which helps massively. With there only being a limited amount of appointments I think the reception staff need to be firmer in turning time wasters away and directing them to the correct place (pharmacy/a&e/self care). Also, they should tell people who repeatedly don't attend their appointments and dont have the decency to advise reception they will be struck off if they don't have a valid reason. Surgery is bright, airy and clean. Chairs could do with being spread out a bit more in my opinion but I'm claustrophobic so perhaps a bit biased. Overall, best doctors surgery I've been too in Heywood and I would recommend. All surgeries seem equally difficult to get appointments so can't hold that against them. As for the occasionally rude receptionist, this is just my experience and how I perceive something that's been said and that will differ from person to person. We all have bad days, we're only human :)

recent_reviews.author: Martha Beatriz Potter
recent_reviews.text: I'm writing this review as a frustrated patient who's had a shocking experience with this practice's service. I phoned at 8am and waited 25-30 minutes just to get an answer. I explained my situation - my consultant had asked them to prescribe more antibiotics for my lung disease, which makes any cold or flu linger and often leads to infections, making me cough uncontrollably and causing incontinence. It's a nightmare. The response seemed straightforward when I spoke to them, but then I got a call an hour later saying I needed to fill in an online form to be triaged. A nice lady helped me with this, but then... nothing. I phoned again at 2pm, was told they'd contact me, and... crickets. It's now 6:47pm. The worst part? This isn't the first time this has happened. I've ended up in A&E twice because their system is so appalling, and both times I've been told "this is something the GP deals with". I rarely use their service, but when I do, it's usually to be told to go to A&E or a walk-in centre. It's infuriating. To anyone considering using this practice, be warned: their system is broken, and it might end up costing you a trip to hospital. Not exactly what you want when you're already feeling well.

recent_reviews.author: Barry
recent_reviews.text: Having recently had a medical issue whilst abroad I was advised to contact my Medical Practice at home. I have been a patient at Greenbank since the 1960s fortunately I have not had to attend on a regular basis however I was pleased to be given a prompt appointment and saw a doctor who was most pleasant and professional and was able to fully interpret the advice I had received whilst abroad. She arranged for me to have an ECG which was done within a week at Greenbank by an equally pleasant and professional person. The results of the ECG were conveyed to me later that day by the the doctor who saw me initiallly and she organised for me to see a specialist at Oldham Hospital within days. I remember that a few years ago I read in the local paper a review of the Greenbank Practice which was rather poor, however after contacting Greenbank I was given the opportunity, a few weeks later, to meet with the leader of the group who had produced that report which illustrated how easy it is to criticise particularly over petty issues. The second follow up report a few months later recognised the true value of the Greenbank practice and the practice was marked up as Good. I have also had recent visits to see the physio at Greenbank with my slight hip problem and again I received prompt and professional help. My golf is just as bad however my hip is on the mend.

recent_reviews.author: J
recent_reviews.text: Very poor experience overall. I was referred by my GP for some tests and given a 6:00pm appointment, which meant taking the afternoon off work. I arrived early to the appointment, but the staff appeared to be preparing to close, despite the clinic not due to shut for another 30 minutes. The lights were off and cleaning staff were already present. When I explained that I had an appointment, the staff seemed confused and told me there were no appointments left for the day. I was questioned in a rather patronising manner about whether I was in the correct place or had the right day, but no one asked for my name or referral details, which surely would have been the most basic step in checking their system and clarifying the situation. I was ultimately turned away without any attempt to investigate further. I contacted my GP the next morning and they confirmed that the appointment had been correctly booked. I am unclear what went wrong, but it is frustrating to now have to rearrange the appointment and potentially take additional time off work.

recent_reviews.author: Madara Luste
recent_reviews.text: If I could give 0 stars, I would. Their incompetence and medical negligence is just unbelievable. Every time I raise a health concern they are just absolutely not interested. I went to seek help with heavy periods. DR Saraf just looked at me and said "what do you want me to do about it?" in the most condescending way possible. Her solution then was to put me on a mini pill. Without once checking my blood pressure before prescribing it or at any point during the 10 months I was on it. Result? I now have to take blood pressure medication for the rest of my life, it's affected my vision and I will need to see a cardiologist once a year for a foreseeable future. Are these meds being reviewed to make sure they are working? Of course not! I also have iron deficiency, due to the heavy periods. Was promised regular blood tests to make sure the levels stay in range. Upon the last request to have them checked I've just had the answer of "they were fine 5 months ago so no need to check" when I had clearly stated I'm getting the same symptoms as the time before when they were extremely low! Communication? Well, now you submit an online form to get an appointment. So far I've submitted 3. 2 got completely no reply. And the 3rd one featured a generic link with no option to respond or raise any further concerns. I could go on about the lack of care and unprofessional attitude, but I genuinely don't believe they will change anything. To anyone considering joining this GP practice, just don't. Might do more harm to your health than good as it's been in my personal experience!

recent_reviews.author: John Gardner
recent_reviews.text: As I approach my 79th summer, I seem to pop more pills than a 1960’s Rolling Stones roadie. Which takes quite a bit of organising in terms of ordering them from my local surgery to keep the supply line flowing. When it comes to being business-like in such matters, on a scale of 1-10, one being chaotic and ten being hyper-efficient, I probably clock in at something like minus 5. That is in contrast to the present Mrs Gardner, who could probably re-organise Manchester United in the morning and the England cricket team in the afternoon. Anyway, the New Year being what it was, I thought I had ordered two sets of tablets from Leesbrook surgery at the dawn of 2026 when the evidence indicates that, in point of fact, I hadn’t. Doh! When this dawned on me earlier today, panic set in for I had consumed my very last Solifenacin tablet last night. We are warned to give plenty of notice when re-ordering prescriptions, particularly at this time of year when the whole NHS is so stretched. So imagine my surprise, delight and admiration when my hasty message to Leesbrook surgery was answered immediately. Together with the ever helpful staff at Well Pharmacy, they arranged for me to have the required medication in my hands this very afternoon. Thank you once again for your brilliant service. Happy New Year from John Gardner

recent_reviews.author: Stacey MacNaught
recent_reviews.text: I appreciate that GP services are incredibly stretched and it can be very difficult to balance offering in advance routine appointments with more urgent on the day appointments. I think this surgery, however, is striking the balance well. The last 3 times I’ve required fairly urgently assessing, I was seen on the same day and treated. Early on this year, after a bout of pneumonia, I suffered a follow up chest infection. I was seen the same day, prescribed antibiotics and the doctor sent a sample from my chest off for testing. I got a call a few days later saying the bacteria on my chest wasn’t the commonly found one and as such would not respond to the antibiotics I was given and he had sent a new prescription to the pharmacy. So instead of seeing me, prescribing something and leaving me to it, the Doctor has followed up, sought more information and then realised my treatment would need changing. Despite the huge time constraints they’re under, they’re still doing a thorough job. I was again recently seen the same day with another potentially urgent requirement. The surgery also now accepts appointment request forms - categorised as urgent and non urgent so you don’t have to wait on the phone. Trying to get through on the phones can be frustrating for sure. But this is, in my view, a Solid example of a clinic that does the best with the resources it has, despite huge patient loads. And doesn’t cut corners on healthcare just to save time. Thorough, understanding and incredibly hard working is my experience of the admin and medical staff I’ve encountered here.

recent_reviews.text: I was registered with this surgery for little over a year, after moving to the Mossley area and the service was absolutely appalling. Even after emailing to raise these issues, nothing was rectified. My messages went unanswered and no attempt was made to resolve the problems. The overall attitude was dismissive and careless, showing complete disregard for patient care. This practice is a disgrace, and I have no idea how it has received any positive reviews. I had no choice but to leave and join a different surgery where professionalism and basic respect are actually shown.

recent_reviews.author: Michael Keating
recent_reviews.text: I felt that my health problems were dismissed and was disappointed and frustrated with the consultation overall. I had registered with the surgery for the GP to consider shared care protocol for ADHD medication prescribed and monitored by a private company I have paid for monthly since January 2025. I'd been advised by the receptionist prior to registering that this would at the least be considered. During my first consultation I was told indefinitely that the practice had a 'blanket rule' against prescribing in this manner. I would have accepted that, as I did with my previous practice, however I feel I was then delivered misinformation that was disheartening and upsetting. The GP told me that 'these private companies will give anybody a diagnosis of ADHD', something which I feel particularly upset and frustrated by. I know for a fact, as a specialist nurse for psychiatry working in primary care that there are many people referred for an ADHD assessment that are not diagnosed but offered alternatives and private companies will make recommendations based on valuable assessments that patients benefit from regardless. For a medical professional to deliver this false information can be especially damaging to somebody in my position, having waited years and paid excessively for support with. I, like many other service users have found relief and in the very least been validated by a diagnosis of ADHD which has answered a lot of questions and provided a pathway to improved wellbeing and hope for the future. The GP also stated that these private companies do not offer a true 'shared care' approach, and that if there are any problems with prescribing in primary care there is no support available from them. I know that this is also false as I have been instructed to remain under the care of the private company and pay for six monthly reviews from the specialists working alongside primary services to ensure safe prescribing and management of medications. The GP also attempted to misinform me that private companies prescribe medications without ensuring safe titration and effective physical health monitoring. Again, I know for a fact that I was sufficiently monitored in terms of bloods, ECG and regular blood pressure and weight reviews since being diagnosed with ADHD in January 2025. In summary, I feel Albion Medical Group have been negligent and failed to deliver individualised care based on service user need. Not only that, but many of the false statements assumed by the GP could have been particularly damaging to vulnerable people with a diagnosis of ADHD, further marginalising people like myself trying to seek support for this disability. If the surgery have a 'blanket rule' against considering shared care protocols for ADHD medication, they should at least ensure the GP's are better informed and work harder not to further dismiss and discredit patients already struggling to access safe support and guidance.

recent_reviews.author: Ali Channa
recent_reviews.text: I have never experienced such an unprofessional and shocking service from any GP practice in my life. Little Town Medical Practice is an absolute joke. We booked an appointment and had to wait three weeks just to be seen – that alone is ridiculous. When I finally arrived for my appointment, I signed in and waited 40–50 minutes past the scheduled time. I became impatient because the appointment time had clearly passed. I asked the receptionist, who told me to “wait another 5–10 minutes and the doctor will see you soon.” After waiting another 10 minutes, she then told me I needed to come back four hours later at 3:30pm. What a joke. I had children to pick up from school, so attending four hours later was impossible. I asked if I could be booked in for the following week instead, and I was told they had no availability at all for the next two weeks. Completely unacceptable and honestly disgusting. To make matters worse, while I was there another patient was arguing with staff because the doctor refused to see her child despite them having an appointment as well. That alone shows this GP treats multiple patients the same way. This is not the first bad experience either. On previous occasions the staff have been extremely rude. When complaining over the phone in the past, I was told things like: “Why don’t you change GP?” “Why don’t you move out of Oldham?” Disgusting attitude. Completely unprofessional. Shows clearly that this GP surgery does not care at all about its patients. Little Town Medical Practice needs serious improvement. People rely on their GP for their health and wellbeing, and this kind of treatment is shameful. I would not recommend this surgery to anyone.

Patients deserve understanding and support, not excuses and obstacles.

recent_reviews.author: Ayanna
recent_reviews.text: I am writing to formally raise serious concerns about the continued poor standard of care and service I have experienced at your practice, which has now reached an unacceptable level. I had a telephone appointment scheduled for today at 10:00 AM to discuss blood test results I have been waiting over two weeks for. The doctor called but let the phone ring for barely a second—so briefly that my phone did not even make a sound before the call ended. This happened twice. By the time I looked at my screen, both calls had already disconnected. It appears these calls were made purely to be logged as “missed” without any genuine effort to reach me. This is not the first time this has happened. During my previous set of blood tests, I experienced the exact same issue with the same doctor. It is becoming a pattern, and I feel unfairly blamed for missing calls that I was never given a fair chance to answer. I contacted reception immediately after the missed calls and was told by one receptionist that the doctor would call me again by 3:00 PM. I waited all afternoon and received no call. When I followed up again, a different receptionist informed me that I would now need to wait until Monday to rebook the appointment. This lack of consistency and the conflicting information from staff is extremely frustrating and unprofessional. Had I been advised at the time of my first call this morning that it was unlikely I would receive a call back, I would have rescheduled immediately while appointments were still available. Instead, I have been left waiting all day, only to be told I now need to start the process again next week. This entire experience follows an already distressing and, frankly, concerning blood test appointment. During the test, the nurse attempted to draw blood from my left arm but was unsuccessful. She then inserted the same needle into my right arm, again unsuccessfully, and a third time into another site using the same needle. I was left with severe bruising due to how aggressive the procedure was. Afterwards, I looked into this and was shocked to learn that reusing the same needle for multiple injection sites is not in line with health and safety regulations. I find it deeply troubling that this occurred, and it has left me feeling not only physically hurt but also incredibly unsafe in your care. All of this is part of a larger issue I have faced at this practice: I have repeatedly had to fight to have my symptoms taken seriously, and even getting basic follow-up care feels like a battle. The reception staff regularly provide conflicting, inaccurate, or vague advice, which only adds to the confusion and stress. At this point, I feel neglected and disrespected as a patient. I will be looking into registering with another GP practice, as I feel the standard of care at this one has significantly declined during my time here. I hope this matter is taken seriously, as it relates not just to poor service, but to potential breaches in clinical safety and patient care standards

recent_reviews.author: A Good Customer
recent_reviews.text: After being on hospital at home for weeks, (because I put off bothering the Dr's) I finished and then went downhill again. Walked to the Dr's early morning, as I was told on the phone to call in the morning - as an extra, but they had no appt. The next day the same, had to dial 111 for help which forced the Dr to call me. I won't say exactly what the Dr said, but they made it clear they couldn't help and to go back to hospital - took them till the evening to call me. I would love to give the Dr's name, but i'll refrain. And yes the place was empty when I went in - where are all the Dr's?? or should I say their patients?? Something a miss here and it's not getting broadcasted. Bring back Dr Milne - the Dr's from a few years ago were amazing which is why I never had to visit. I get one problem and it's taking months - this is after decades never going to the Dr's. Oh be we're here to give you a flu or covid jab - we get paid for that. We should all go to the chemists for them. If Dr's don't want to work - leave or close the place. Something smells I know that.

Literally my colon and uterus are glued together and I have growths everywhere. Had I had a competent person tend to me I could have gotten better treatment sooner. Shame on him.

recent_reviews.author: Cece Sinclair
recent_reviews.text: This place is let down by DR Dadah. Legitimately the worst Dr I've ever dealt with. I primarily attend the practice due to bad mental health. My usual GP Dr Proctor is excellent, but there have been times I've had to see a different GP. Every time I've seen Dr Dadah I always end up having a panic attack and am left feeling belittled. Today during an appointment I told him how he was making me feel and he proceeded to tell me I was projecting and it was my issue and I shouldn't be placing it on him. recent_reviews.author: Jeanette Neilson
recent_reviews.text: I have been with this practice since moving to Gatley 28 years ago. Both my children , now adults were cared for at Gatley medical practice and the same for my husband and I. In our current climate of underfunding and lack of resources this practice continues to provide an excellent and exceptional service to its patients. I have always got through to the practice and have managed to get an appointment 99% of the time. Reception staff have been helpful and friendly. I have always been treated with courtesy and dignity having a long-term condition. I do think people should be realistic. Use the pharmacy or 111 for advice. Urgent problems go to ED. The practice is not a walk in and expectations that someone should get a same day appointment then get annoyed because they can't is unfair on an already over stretched service doing their best for the local community. Its a 10/10 from me. Thank you Gatley Medical Centre

recent_reviews.author: Helisa Bagheri
recent_reviews.text: I am extremely disappointed with the service at this GP practice. Over the years, both my children and I have been misdiagnosed multiple times, leading to serious consequences for our health. One particularly alarming experience involved a senior GP dismissing my concerns about perimenopausal symptoms. Despite expressing that I suspected I was entering perimenopause, she laughed and told me I was too young, completely disregarding that perimenopause can occur at various ages. She prescribed me the wrong medication, which worsened my symptoms to the point that I almost ended up in a mental health crisis.When I reported this to her, she casually offered antidepressants and didn’t even arrange a follow-up to check on my well-being. I had to take matters into my own hands and consult a private GP, who immediately confirmed I was perimenopausal and prescribed HRT. My symptoms improved almost instantly. This kind of negligence is unacceptable, and I have completely lost trust in this practice. I’ve even witnessed doctors Googling information in front of me, which makes me wonder—why bother going to the GP if I can just look things up myself? It seems they are only useful for minor issues like colds or flu. I would not recommend trusting them with anything beyond that.

recent_reviews.author: Sabina
recent_reviews.text: I went for a dermatology appointment at Handforth Health Centre. From the moment I entered the door, I found the personnel not very helpful. Then, I was taken by a very unpleasant nurse (of Asian origin, I think) to see my dermatologist. She was very moody and stayed with me during the appointment. I came with a mole I was worried about, so the dermatologist suggested checking all my other moles. However, I needed to take off my clothes in front of him without any separate curtains for privacy. The nurse was sitting on a chair next to the door in the meantime during all apointment. I felt really rushed taking my clothes off and throughout the entire appointment. Then, when the dermatologist finished the examination, I wanted to ask a few questions, but after my second question, the nurse opened the door to signal that the appointment was over and I had to leave. I have never experienced anything like that with the NHS or any medical organization anywhere in the world. It was an absolutely horrible experience.

recent_reviews.author: Mickey Puri
recent_reviews.text: I had been told by a friend that St Johns was one of the very few surgeries that was doing something to find out if Statins would suit you. So I called them re this. A doctor called back same day but he said he was a Locum and was not aware of any test as this. Then at 7pm same day, Vanessa, the Practice Manager called me and said there had been a trial running that looked into this, and the trial was ending the next day. So she agreed to put me down for it and next day I took part in the trial. So its great that St Johns is taking part in such initiatives, and I was hugely grateful to Vanessa for calling me well outside normal surgery times and booking me onto the trial, that too in a Christmas Week. Very impressive and Well Done!

recent_reviews.author: Simon G
recent_reviews.text: Some good and bad experiences here. Was seen last year by a female doctor here who diagnosed me with anxiety and depression. I was referred for CBT treatment. The therapist, after many hours of talking therapy suggested that I may be suffering from a neurodiversity condition. I mentioned this to my GP on my next check in and was practically laughed at. The response was basically that we all experience these symptoms. I was embarrassed and didn’t raise the issue again. I was placed on a high dose of anti depressants and sent on my way. I’ve now stopped the medication abruptly as I am still experiencing the same problems - withdrawal is hell but I have no desire to return to this GP to revisit what was discussed with my therapist and have nowhere else to turn. Looking to transfer to a new GP to get the help I need

recent_reviews.author: Chuanjie Zhou
recent_reviews.text: I have great concerns about this medical centre, and I have no issue with doctors, but their reception team was very rude. You will never expect them to give you a smile. We have made an urgent appointment 9 am today for our granddaughter, who has had a bad cough with a running nose. We arrived at the medical centre 9:10am and at that time only one receptionist attended, but was continuously using the phone. We were waiting patiently for over five minutes until she finished her phone call. Then she told us that the appointment was invalid because we missed the appointment by over 15minutes. We tried to argue with her that we arrived at 9:10 am and the appointment should be valid. Suddenly, five receptionists appeared at the reception desk, showing a very aggressive manner, and one of the receptionists even threatened to call the police. I have to say, this reception team is arrogant, rude, and has a total lack of empathy for the patients. The management team should look into restructuring the reception team! I have checked all 53 Google reviews of this medical centre, and 26 out of 53 were one star, with an average score of 2.6. So far, this 2.6 score is the lowest within Greater Manchester that I have ever seen. 16 of 53 were complaints about their receptionists, which should tell you something!

recent_reviews.author: helene Manchester
recent_reviews.text: I have been at the Village Surgery since around 2007 and after reading the reviews on Google, I thought I had to try to rectify the records as I believe they should get a full 5 stars. The doctors are second to none. They are part of this new generation of professionals who are open to their patients' opinion, take time to listen to their concerns and expectations and go to the extent of reseaching on topics if needs be. I have always felt that they actually enjoyed their profession. My friends based in other surgeries can't believe the help I get from my doctors. The office manager is very capable; some of the receptionists can be a bit unpolished but generally, the service at the desk is very good. The building is clean and welcoming. Parking is not always easy but arriving a good 10 minutes before the appointment can help as people come but also vacate quite quickly.

recent_reviews.author: Kong Ng
recent_reviews.text: We have always been with this GP under our postcode area (WA14/15), but they changed their catchment area quietly without any notice. Suddenly, we were no longer within their coverage. When my wife needed to see a doctor, the NHS app still allowed her to book an appointment. However, when she arrived, instead of being asked about her symptoms, the first question was, “Why are you here at this GP?” As an organisation responsible for safeguarding the health of local residents, it is disappointing that they chose to turn away an unwell patient rather than provide care and then explain that her address is no longer within their service area.

recent_reviews.author: Jenny
recent_reviews.text: Monday, 27th October I spoke to Sara at 08:12 I said I would like to book an appointment for my husband Roger. He had difficulty breathing and his peakflow was very low, and a back cough.She said I can't book a telephone appointment. She said I had to book online which I did. I requested a telephone call after 12pm. I also requested that they phone Roger on his home landlines as he doesn't have a smart phone. I received a reminder message showing up on phone at 17:00 saying can Roger come in today to the surgery at 15:20 Luckily my husband phoned the surgery at 11:15 to remind them to use the landlines and luckily he found out the appointment was in person and he was able to go in good time. The fact that I had no knowledge of the appointment to 17:00 meant my husband would have missed his appointment had he not phoned the surgery at 11:15

recent_reviews.author: WAYNE LARGE
recent_reviews.text: Possibly one of the most disappointing experiences I’ve ever had with senior doctors. After being told by district nurses and undertakers that I could collect a death certificate to register my parent’s passing, I arrived at the practice only to be informed that the procedure had changed. Neither the nurses nor the detailed NHS leaflet I was given reflected this change, leading to unnecessary confusion at an already difficult time. When I asked to speak to the manager, I was instead met by her secretary, who I initially assumed was the manager until informed otherwise. Despite requesting the manager again and asking for the new procedure in writing, I was then redirected to a junior doctor. They asked me to fill out a form I had already completed with the district nurse, which then had to be emailed. To make matters worse, I later received a call from a senior doctor accusing me of upsetting and being rude to staff—a claim that was both unfounded and deeply upsetting. This same doctor, during a previous home visit, did not even know my parent’s name. On the phone, her tone was condescending and defensive when I questioned her. Over recent months, during an incredibly emotional period, I have consistently found this practice to be unhelpful, lacking in empathy, and frequently contradictory in their communication. Sensitive matters were often discussed in the crowded reception area, which felt completely inappropriate and disrespectful. This experience added unnecessary stress during bereavement, and I sincerely hope the practice takes steps to improve their procedures and communication in the future.

recent_reviews.text: I phoned this practice ahead of my appointment to notify them that I might be 5mins late due to an ongoing meeting. The receptionist Lesley claimed that I didn’t have an appointment and that I was left a voicemail. After trying to explain to her for what felt like hours that I returned the call to confirm my appointment which was in fact NOT cancelled ,the conversation wasn’t going anywhere and there was no apology for wasting my time. Poor customer service as well as an “I don’t care” attitude. After reading through these reviews,I’ve understood that many other patients are subject to this rude behaviour too. Businesses should review job performances based on competency and not how long they’ve worked there for- especially with FOH staff. From my own experience, I understand that receptionist jobs can be extremely challenging but for a middle aged woman to be so ‘fed up with it’ as so to speak, maybe it’s time for her to leave.

recent_reviews.author: Jodie Leigh
recent_reviews.text: I’d be apprehensive to say this practice even deserves one star. I had been registered here for the past approximately 15 years and throughout attended this practice for multiple ongoing problems which I feel have been ignored and unseen to despite countless visits. The main problem is not the qualified healthcare staff but the overall system and management, I work in healthcare myself and understand that sometimes no matter how well patients are treated by staff they are still failed by the declining system of the NHS. Although I have felt ignored by some practitioners whose names I cannot remember, nurse Karen and mental health practitioner Ian have been great and have always listened to my health issues thoroughly. The reception staff answer calls with rude manner (I can’t say all as I have had kind receptionists previously but the majority of time not) and they appear uninterested in answering your queries and concerns. The appointment availability is unacceptable, attempting to arrange an on the day appointment at 8am often leaves you without one and trying to pre book an appointment leaves you with a 3-7 week wait and there is no acknowledgement of urgent symptoms. Sometimes they’ll tell you a GP will contact you over the phone on the day to assess your symptoms and then no one rings you all day from the practice. The final straw for me was when I rang last week describing tachycardia, feeling faint and CHEST PAIN and they told me they had no appointments for 4 weeks, neither did they advise me on what to do or where else to go for urgent medical attention. I have since changed practice and they have been a huge improvement.

recent_reviews.author: Diane Moss
recent_reviews.text: I took my twelve year old granddaughter to Hopwood medical centre yesterday (15th December) our appt was 11am, we finally got to see the dr at 11.50 ( I know they are busy). He said she had dry eyes and written on a piece of paper what to get from the chemist. I said she is 12 ( although she looks about 9) are you not going to give her a script, I asked him twice and he said no, you can buy over the counter, I said but she is 12. He said ' my supervisor will ask me why I gave a script out when it can be purchased OTC' , again I said she is 12. I went into the chemist, the lady said have they not given you a script, I said no and I told her my granddaughter was 12. £6.50 it was for these eye drops which I probably could have bought at Morrisons for less. My gripe is. If I as pensioner I was told to buy something OTC, even though though we are entitled, I would have paid it but a 12 year old. Disgusted with this practice if that is how they work. I think they need to look at who is entitled to what . End of gripe

recent_reviews.text: Me and my whole family have been using Dr Ghafoor for the last 10+ years.The practise used to be really good and now the service has completely gone down hill. The recepionists are rude and couldn't care less (why work in Health Care then?) The pratice have made ordering prescriptions online now, which is fine but then trying to order a medication which is not on the list (Needed a blue inhaler for my Asthma) is such a process, loads of questions to answer which is time consuming to then be told is under review and to follow it up in 2 days after 2pm. Follow it up by calling the practice after 2 days to be told the Doctor hasn't checked it yet, call back after 5pm same day....Call back after 5pm to be asked a load of questions about how I use my medication and the woman sounded very hostile on the phone like I've done something wrong (why ask all those questions online then?) and then get told to call back the following day after 5pm. I will be looking to leave this practice asap and in due course move over every other person in my family to a practice that actually cares for it's patients and wants to actually help people. Thanks for reading

recent_reviews.author: James Stridgen
recent_reviews.text: My son was advised by two separate locum doctors on two occasions at the surgery, to apply to ADHD 360 for an assessment for ADHD as the waiting list on the national health was 8 years. He was given the organisations name and address then contacted them for an assessment. We (his parents) borrowed the £1000 required fee and he was assessed for between 1 and 4 hours by ADHD 360. His results showed that he scored 99% symptoms on every test and was told that there were only 7% of the population with such scores. Obviously now having a diagnosis he made an appointment to see his GP at Yorkshire street where he was told that they could/would not prescribe the vital medication he needs to live a normal independent life and relieve his symptoms. He was told that because he went to a private company (as advised) then he had to pay for private prescriptions. As he is currently receiving statutory sick pay there is no way he can do this, nor as pensioners can we. What can we do next please ?

recent_reviews.author: Dominic Keefe
recent_reviews.text: Some of the doctors here are more thoughtful than others but overall they reflect institutional neglect. I'm dealing with a disabling and frightening chronic condition that has been poorly investigated and diagnosed by the NHS and this health center. Tests have always comeback within their very broad definition of 'normal' and they refuse to apply any further clinical consideration to a patients' actual clinical picture. I asked for my medical records and I still haven't received the requested information three months later. I've complained but received no response. One receptionist a month ago completely ignored me. Then she dealt with me as if it was an inconvenience. The online triage system is now a grim joke. It frequently suspends the option to make an appointment for a week or more, and then every alternative method of contact filters you back to it. The clinic is at the forefront of a modern dysfunctional NHS where compassion disappeared decades ago. The patient comes very last in its considerations and it merely a source of LHA funding. Addendum : I am now discovering that the causes that I suggested for my illness and was laughed out of the surgery with ('Dr' Yazicci actually laughed at them) are indeed the issue and I am now self medicating with considerbale success. The dimissal of my theories by this surgery has cost me years of my life as I didn't act on it. Any attempt to complain to them is water off a duck's back to them. I've since changed surgeries. When I mentioned I was going to this, this one became even less responsive and more dismissive.

recent_reviews.text: As of October 1st 2025 gov.uk made the announcement that patients in the UK, will be able to request appointments online throughout the day, rather than calling their surgery or visiting in person. Speaking as a person who works full time and begins at 7:30am, making an appointment outside of works time is pretty much impossible and, if you are fortunate enough to get an appointment, it's often a month away and in working hours. Online booking is essential for those who are employed, and in order to access this it has to be operational. Surely nearly 3 years to get it back up and running is plenty of time?

recent_reviews.author: Betty Boop
recent_reviews.text: Have been a patient here for years. Such a shame that it is now so difficult to get an appointment. There is no continuity with regards to doctors and if you're lucky to get an appointment, you are essentially a stranger each time you go. You can't get through at 8am when the phone lines open. You are told that you can attend at 8am to make an appointment in person, but even then, due to the limited number of appointments available (lack of actual doctors) i have had times where I have attended at 8am and by the time I am seen, all appointments have gone. It seems a totally ridiculous way to run a doctor's surgery. The nurse practitioner is abrupt and rude and acts like the cost of a prescription comes out of her own pocket. When told that there were a couple of things that needed to be mentioned to her ( due to having had to wait a good few weeks to get an appointment) she responded by saying that she only had time to discuss one thing!!! Roisin the practice nurse is lovely and the most helpful member of staff at the surgery, and also seems to be the most overworked staff there too. The reception staff are generally as helpful as they can be but without actual doctors to see patients, the surgery would seem to be struggling.

recent_reviews.author: Vikrant Kalukhe
recent_reviews.text: I visited the practice for an in-person appointment to obtain a fit note while suffering from flu symptoms, including a high fever. I had made significant effort to attend despite feeling very unwell. Upon arrival, I was informed by the receptionist that the appointment was actually a telephone consultation, which was not indicated when the booking was made or confirmed. I politely pointed this out, explaining that it appeared to be an administrative error, and suggested it might help to flag this to prevent similar mix-ups for other patients in the future (e.g., someone travelling unnecessarily while ill). Unfortunately, instead of acknowledging the mistake or apologising, the receptionist repeated that I did not need to wait in the surgery for the call – raising her voice and speaking slowly and loudly on the second occasion. This felt highly patronising and dismissive, especially when I was already feeling extremely unwell and vulnerable. In the end, the journey was wasted, and I left without the consultation proceeding as expected. Clearer communication about appointment types and better handling of patient feedback when errors occur would greatly improve the experience here.

recent_reviews.author: Amanda Neville
recent_reviews.text: A masterclass in how not to run a GP surgery. Reception staff appear to have taken on the role of clinicians, routinely dismissing concerns, deciding what does and does not warrant medical attention, and frequently redirecting patients to A&E or out-of-hours services for minor or ongoing issues. One wonders when this became part of their job description. GP consultations offer little improvement. Complex medical conditions, mental health concerns, and written recommendations from specialists are met with indifference or ignored altogether. Listening appears optional; empathy entirely absent. Complaints are treated with the same enthusiasm as patient care — acknowledged, if at all, then quietly disregarded. Patients are spoken to in a patronising manner and left feeling foolish for seeking help. If you are looking for accessible, patient-centred care, this is not the place. If, however, you enjoy being dismissed, redirected elsewhere, and made to feel like an inconvenience, this surgery may be exactly what you’re looking for.

recent_reviews.author: Deborah Walton
recent_reviews.text: I have had a horrendous experience being registered with this group practice. I made a complaint about a senior admin worker who denied receiving 3 letters from my solicitor after waiting 12mths for a copy of my gp notes . Then my Gp notes were destroyed vindictivly I am amazed that the practice manager didn't know it was gross Misconduct and a criminal offence to tamper, alter or fix a patients notes. I know this by comments passed to me at a practice managers meeting. I had no option but to report this to the GMC who passed it to NHS England to investigate. My case was to serious for them to investigate as they should do because I named 2 Gp s who I had apts with and went in, sat down. The Gp looked at his screen and didn't speak when I told him my reason for going to see a Gp, he totally ignored me and after what felt like 30 mins of silence I got up and left his room. I had no idea Dr's behaved this way and happened twice with 2 Gp's. NHS England conducted a corrupt investigation without a single meeting with me. I found out 12mths later that the GMC worked with NHS England on this investigation, they don't work together. All this came to the senior Gp at the practice who was responsible for the surgery, I now know he took early retirement before the investigation got going. Ever since I have been treated very badly by every Gp I have seen at several practices. I am denied Healthcare, treatment and medication across the board even mental health services have been closed to me. I have been set up by mental health nurses who requested a urine sample under the order of a consultant. The drug test they did came up positive for every substance you can think of but my prescribed medication didn't show up on the drug test, codeine and pregabalin are both controlled drugs and medication I take every day. Think this proves it was all staged and a set up, you don't expect this from a mental health nurse. Had I taken any kind of class A drugs I wouldn't have given anyone a urine sample. I was left bent in half with horrific back pain the Gp practice I was registered with Mark Street Surgery refused to review my pain relief or increase it. I am now disabled for the rest of my life and under a spinal surgeon at Salford with a life curve of my spine. I could go on forever I am now registered in littleborough and denied any kind of Healthcare Treatment and medication. Just today I've been denied antibiotics for a chest infection and have COPD. They are trying to kill me off for daring to make a complaint. I am advising everyone not to make any complaints against any Gp's if you do your life will be turned into a living hell just as mine has. If you do you will get invented diagnoses, lies out and out lies all on your care summary and cannot be removed, only they do remove notes and letters and remove all names of Dr's and nurses from your Gp notes this is tampering again with my life. My whole life and the birth of my Boys has been wiped out how dare they do this to me ? I have a right to complain I cannot sit back and take being labeled a druggie, this is now one step to far I've been given no option but to go to the Nursing and Midwifery council and The royal college of nurses and midwives. I can't be punished anymore than I have been and still taking this off Gp's and bardoc Dr's, who put the cuff on to do my BP and don't inflate it they then walk out of my home without a word. A Gp at the practice I am registered with looked in my ear after earache for 2wks and bleeding from inside and said it was OK Really ?? I also had a swelling under my arm and lumps he failed to examine me and have a family history of breast cancer. He smirked at me in a very sick way, he's training to be a Gp. District Nurses refuse me compression bandages requested by my vascular surgeon but then go on to lie and document I couldn't tolerate them. I am totally disgusted with all of them I am now self managing leg ulcers because they refuse me home visits and dressings. Don't complain its not worth it.

recent_reviews.author: Sandeep Tandon
recent_reviews.text: I ordered my repeat prescription via the app several days ago. When I attended the pharmacy, I was told the prescription had not been authorised by the doctor. On Thursday, I attended the surgery and was informed by the receptionist that the particular doctor was “not in”. I explained the urgency and asked for the prescription to be pushed through. I was then assured that my medication would be ready to collect from the pharmacy on Saturday morning. Today (Saturday 17/01/26), I attended the pharmacy at 1pm, only to find that it was closed. Both the pharmacy and the GP surgery are now closed. As of today, I have completely run out of my prescribed medication, including Ramipril and Atorvastatin. I have disabilities and suffer from high blood pressure, and being without this medication places my health at risk. I am extremely concerned that the online prescription service is being promoted, yet it is ineffective if prescriptions are not authorised in a timely manner. The system only works if doctors take responsibility for approving patients’ medication. I would like this matter urgently reviewed, an explanation provided as to how this situation was allowed to occur, and assurances that this does not happen again. I also request immediate advice on how I can obtain my medication as soon as possible. I look forward to your prompt response. Yours faithfully, S
